commandDescriptions.strengths: What I bring to a team

sections.title: Introduction
paragraphs: I'm a software engineer and technical leader building complex products with .NET, Python, and JavaScript/TypeScript. I connect product thinking with hands-on engineering—from understanding the problem to supporting the product in production.

sections.title: The person behind the code.
paragraphs: I'm a product-minded software engineer with more than a decade of experience building complex products, primarily with .NET, Python, and JavaScript/TypeScript.
For over five years, I've combined hands-on engineering with technical leadership, working closely with developers, QA, product, and architecture stakeholders.
I care about understanding the problem, choosing the right technology, and building systems that remain reliable and maintainable as they grow.
I lead by example, support the people around me, and value clean code, testing, and continuous improvement.
Recently, I've been exploring how AI-assisted engineering can improve delivery speed and quality without lowering architectural or testing standards.

sections.title: Selected experience.
paragraphs: A few selected engagements from my career—not a complete work history. These examples span payment systems and dental software, with employers and clients shown separately.

items.title: Reliable payment systems
items.subtitle: Technical leadership & hands-on delivery
paragraphs: Developing and upgrading .NET payment solutions for Global Payments on a platform that processes billions of dollars annually. The work supports high-volume, mission-critical financial operations, where reliability, scalability, and safe releases matter.
Cross-functional delivery alongside engineering, QA, product, and architecture stakeholders.
bullets: Lead work from requirements and solution design through testing, release coordination, and post-release support.
Establish maintainable architecture, code quality, and testing practices.
Mentor engineers and collaborate with globally distributed teams.

items.title: Engineering in three dimensions
items.subtitle: Dental CAD/CAM software
paragraphs: .NET software for Frame Design, Anatomy Design, and TRIOS, working with complex architectures and algorithms for 3D-space problems.
bullets: Worked across three dental software products.
Developed algorithms for geometric problems in 3D space.
3Shape was a client of Inscale in Skopje.

sections.title: More than a technology stack.
paragraphs: Good engineering connects the product, the people, and the details that make it work.

items.title: Start with the problem
items.subtitle: Product thinking
paragraphs: Understand who we're building for and why. Connect technical choices to the user's problem, not the other way around.

items.title: Lead from the work
items.subtitle: Hands-on leadership
paragraphs: Stay close to the technology, support the team, and help people do their best work. Lead by example.

items.title: Build for what comes next
items.subtitle: Architecture & quality
paragraphs: Clean code, thoughtful architecture, testing, and continuous improvement make complex systems easier to live with.

items.title: Keep learning. Keep improving.
items.subtitle: Adaptability & practical AI
paragraphs: Choose the right tools for the problem. Explore AI-assisted delivery without compromising engineering judgment.

sections.title: From operational problem to maintained product.

items.title: Understand
items.subtitle: Find the right problem
paragraphs: Clarify users, business goals, current problems, constraints, and what success looks like. Use quick AI-assisted UI prototypes to test understanding before committing to a solution.

items.title: Architect
items.subtitle: Give the solution structure
paragraphs: Shape the product, data model, integrations, permissions, workflows, and interface direction around the problem and its constraints.

items.title: Build
items.subtitle: Turn intent into working software
paragraphs: Deliver the frontend, backend, integrations, and supporting infrastructure the product needs, including mobile or desktop where appropriate.

items.title: Launch & improve
items.subtitle: The release is a beginning
paragraphs: Test, deploy, monitor, maintain, and improve the product using evidence from real users and production operation.

sections.title: Built to learn. Shared to help.
paragraphs: A selection of my pet projects—not the full list. These projects were built before AI-assisted coding and written manually. Small experiments, useful tools, and learning in public, built outside the day job.

items.title: Coding Problems
items.subtitle: A practical algorithms notebook
paragraphs: Python solutions and curated resources for learning algorithms and data structures. Written to make the ideas approachable across languages.

items.title: Virus Spreading
items.subtitle: Making an invisible problem visible
paragraphs: An interactive vanilla JavaScript simulation exploring how different parameters affect spreading and flattening the curve. An educational visualization, not an epidemiological prediction tool.

items.title: SlediPratki
items.subtitle: One place to follow a package
paragraphs: A Chrome extension built to track postal shipments in Macedonia, with background updates and notifications. A project from my open-source collection; current service availability is not guaranteed.

sections.title: Discipline, one step at a time.
paragraphs: Running is how I practice discipline: showing up early in the morning or late in the evening, even when motivation is low.
Away from the run, I'm usually learning something new about engineering, technology, or product development.

sections.title: Let's build something useful.
paragraphs: Have an interesting problem, a product idea, or a different perspective? I'd be happy to connect.
